links.reason: Neelakesi 76 counts seven (ஏழாய் அவை) spreading into eighty-four hundred thousand, while Manimekalai 6:181 only lists எண் வகை நரகரும் in a catalogue of beings, a count of kinds of beings rather than of hells; the sectarian difference is real but thin. Teaches adds 'seven earths stacked below the world', which verse 76 does not say.
links.text_issue: Neelakesi 76 lines 3-4 (முழுச்செவி கிண்ணர்கள், முவ்வாதம்) are hard to construe.

links.reason: Kannaki says she went to heaven by former good deeds (மேற் செய் நல் வினையின் விண்ணவர்ச் சென்றேம்) and that when that deed ends (அவ் வினை இறுதியின்) the sin of anger will reach her; the venba makes her the guest of heaven's women (விண்ணக மாதர்க்கு விருந்து) as a final honour. Qualifies fits: the later epic makes the heavenly reward temporary.

The shared item is real and distinctive: Puram 9 swears by நெடியோன் நன்னீர்ப் பஃறுளி மணலினும் பலவே, and Silap 11:19-20 has the sea take பஃறுளி யாற்றுடன் ... குமரிக் கோடும். But this is a shared name/image, not a development; and the Purananuru gains nothing specific from a later legend ('sharpening its wish' is vague).

Manimekalai 27:180-182 gives the Jain triad in each moment (ஓர் கணத்தின் கண்ணே தோற்றமும் நிலையும் கேடும்), and Neelakesi 392 has the Buddhist ask what bears கெடுவன தோன்றுவ நிற்பன if they are qualities (குணமென்றியேல்). The Jain epic stages the rival school's actual objection to the same doctrine the Buddhist epic only reports.

Madhavi's last song (பொய்ச்சூள் பொறுக்க என்று மாக்கடல் தெய்வம் நின் மலர்அடி வணங்குதும்) does answer Kovalan's charge (அரியசூள் பொய்த்தார் அறன்இலர்), but a plea for pardon and a condemnation are not incompatible claims, so tension is the wrong type. Teaches calls it 'the same broken oath', but they are two songs about different fictional lovers.
links.text_issue: Line 284 கனலில் may be a corruption of கானலில்.

links.reason: The anklet set aside (அணிசிலம்பு ஒழிய, 4:47) and the anklet offered (சிலம்புஉள கொண்மின், 9:73) are the same object, a real image link. But 9:67-79 does not answer or fulfil the ornament-stripping; teaches' claim that the unworn state 'is what lets it become the capital' is not in the Tamil.

The ball song hails தென்னன் and தேவரார மார்பன், and Kannaki has just called the Pandya தீதிலன் and Indra's guest (தேவர்கோன் தன்கோயில் நல்விருந்தாயினான்), so the juxtaposition is real. But the Indra-necklace epithet is an old Pandya title (cf. 11:24), and the Vazhthu songs praise the crowned kings in turn, so 'only because she has called him blameless can the women hail him' overstates the Tamil.

The Kural calls stealth காரறிவாண்மை, a dark knowledge; the goldsmith's lecture sets out thieves' eight aids as a lore (மந்திரம் தெய்வம் மருந்தே நிமித்தம்...). The epic applies rather than limits the couplet, so qualifies fits poorly, and the link rests on a shared theme of theft-as-skill.

Neelakesi mocks the Buddhist monk who still cooks dye (துவரடுதி பூவடுதி சோறடலே முனிந்தாயோ) and Sivavakkiyar the Saiva yogi who leaves his wife and begs (தேவியை அலையவிட்டு ... பருக்கைகேட்டு); the opposite charges are a neat contrast. But the targets are different orders, so neither limits the other; it is a parallel satire, not a qualification.

In Neelakesi 57 கூற்றம் is only a simile for the demoness's cruelty (கூற்றம் போல்வதோர் கொடுமையை உடையவள்), and she yields to the sage's tapas fire (அருந்தவ அழல் எனை அடும்); Kural 269 promises that tapas leaps death itself (கூற்றம் குதித்தலும் கைகூடும்). The link stretches a simile into Death, so the gains clause 'the outcome the Kural promised' is untrue.

Kannaki calls her anger அடு சினப் பாவம் whose fruit will reach her after heaven (அவ் வினை இறுதியின் ... எய்துதல் ஒழியாது), applying Kural 305's தன்னையே கொல்லுஞ் சினம் across births. This extends the rule to provoked anger and a later life, which is develops more than qualifies.

Neelakesi 275 says covering the limbs (உறுப்பெல்லாம் மறைக்கின்றாய்) shows an unfirm mind and that the eyes must be guarded (கண்ணன்றோ உள்ளத்தைக் கலக்குவன அவை காவாய்); Kural 126 is about drawing in the five senses like a tortoise. Neelakesi makes no tortoise allusion, and equating hiding the limbs with cloth to the tortoise's limbs stretches both; on the senses the two simply agree.

The drunk does reason with the ascetic (கொலையும் உண்டோ ... விளை பூந் தேறலில்), the reverse of Kural 929's களித்தானைக் காரணம் காட்டுதல். The reversal is a clever observation but a shared topic; the Kural does not gain from a comic scene, and 'the futility runs both ways' is not what the epic shows.

Kundalakesi 1 opens முன்றான் பெருமைக்கண் நின்றான், and Neelakesi 179 takes the word up: முன்னெனப் படுவதுதான் முதலில்லாத் தடுமாற்றம், then poses a dilemma. The Jain refutes the Buddhist invocation's own claim on a defensible reading; tension fits.
links.text_issue: Neelakesi 179 lines 2 and 4 are hard to construe; the first horn of the dilemma is reconstructed.

links.reason: The same witnesses report the same ascent twice, under the vengai (கான வேங்கைக் கீழோர் காரிகை, 25:57; பொலம்பூ வேங்கை, 0:4), first to the renouncer prince and then to the reigning king, and 25:61-62 adds that they do not know her (யார்மகள் கொல்லோ ... அறியேம்). Frame and Vanchi book answer each other, which is more than plot sequence.

Kural 1213 keeps the woman alive by seeing him in dreams (கனவினால் காண்டலின் உண்டென் உயிர்); Madhavi's woman cannot sleep and asks the sleeping neythal whether in its dream (எய்தும் கனவினுள்) it sees the cruel man. The song names a real limit to the couplet's consolation, sleeplessness, and both gains hold.

The youthful vow (மைத்துனன் மனையாள் மறு பிறப்பு ஆகுவேன் இப் பிறப்பு இவனொடும் கூடேன்) is kept and restated at sixty (ஆறு ஐந்து இரட்டி யாண்டு; இப் பிறப்பு ஆயின் யான் நின் அடி அடையேன் அப் பிறப்பு...), and they do charity together (அவன் அவளுடன் செய்த நல் அறம்). The later unit fulfils the earlier vow; 'forty years' is an inference, not in the Tamil.

The verbal contact is strong: Kural 334 நாளென ... உயிர் ஈரும் வாளது and Kundalakesi 10 நாளடி இடுதல் ... நம்முயிர் பருகுங் கூற்றின் வாளின்வாய், and the fragment adds the condemned man's walk. But this is a bridge and it carries no gains clauses at all, so it cannot be graded sound as written.

Both verses answer a Buddhist defence of meat-eating by intention: 260 says karma attaches to the eater when the butcher cuts (கூடுமோ கன்மம்), 344 that the sellers kill for the price (விலை வாணிகர்). The second does develop the first, but both verses are obscure in key lines and the 'butcher' reading of 260 is uncertain, so the consistent-case claim needs a generous reading.
links.text_issue: Neelakesi 260 இல்லில்வாழ்பேய் and 344 line 3 ஓவெனு முன் are obscure.

links.reason: Kural 324 defines the good way as the path that keeps not killing anything in view (யாதொன்றும் கொல்லாமை சூழும் நெறி); Kavunthi on the actual road warns that a careless step may harm the crab and snail (பொறிமாண் அலவனும் நந்தும் போற்றாது ... தாழ்தரு துன்பம்). The epic literalises the path metaphor and shows யாதொன்றும் reaching creatures underfoot.

Kural 92 ranks sweet speech above a glad gift; Kural 225 ranks relieving hunger above enduring it. These rank different pairs and make no incompatible claim; the 'hungry person's view' in teaches is speculation, not a reading of either couplet.

Kannaki names வல்வினை வந்து உருத்தகாலை and calls herself கடுவினையேன் (24:5-6), and the hill women say she burned Koodal கோமுறை நீங்க (24:111): two causes in two voices, a real observation. But neither limits the other, so qualifies does not fit, and the note's 'her own cruel deed as the cause of Madurai's ruin' reads more into கடுவினையேன் than line 6 states.

The narrator puts ஊழ்வினைக் கடைஇ உள்ளம் துரப்ப (10:4) behind the departure, which fits Kural 380's ஊழிற் பெருவலி யாவுள. But the plan to recover wealth that teaches turns on is not in this unit (it is 9:74-75 or line 51), and the couplet speaks of a counter-plan that fate outruns, not of a plan that carries fate; the pairing is close to illustration.

The kings flee in the guise of ascetics (சடையினர் உடையினர் சாம்பற் பூச்சினர் ...) as Kural 586's spy goes துறந்தார் படிவத்தராகி: the shared device is real. But the epic adds no limit to the couplet, and teaches' 'it works because no one strikes a man who looks like a renouncer' is not in the Tamil, which says only they went where they wished.
links.text_issue: விச்சைக் கோலத்து (230) is uncertain in sense.

links.reason: Aputhiran dies holding the purpose of sustaining lives (தணியா மன் உயிர் தாங்கும் கருத்தொடு, 14:102) and is born to rule Savakam; in 25:100-109 the minister says the land had no rain for twelve years before his birth and since then வானம் பொய்யாது ... உறு பசி அறியா. The later unit fulfils the purpose held at death.
links.text_issue: 14:103-104 attachment of சாவகம் ஆளும் தலைத் தாள் வேந்தன் is unclear.

links.reason: The patikam's kuravar call the ascent a wonder (இறும்பூது போலும்), while 23:191-192 has Kannaki under the flowering vengai lament தீத்தொழிலாட்டியேன் யான் before the heavenly car takes her. The pair contrasts the outsiders' marvel with the heroine's guilt, which neither shows alone.

The shared phrase is real: Silap 6:159-160 கரிகால் வளவன் தண்பதம் கொள்ளும் தலைநாள் and Akam 376:5-6 கரிகால் காணத் தண்பதம் கொண்டு. But that the epic's simile carries a 'buried memory of loss' is a generous reading, and the Akananuru gains nothing about its own festival from a simile describing a different shore crowd.

Kavunthi's fast is told in one line with her question என்னோடு இவர் வினை உருத்ததோ (27:82-83), and Perunjeralathan sits north ashamed of a back wound (புறப்புண் நாணி ... வடக்கு இருந்தனன்). The shared act of dying by fasting is a theme; the epic gives no sign of shame or honour code, so 'carries the honour code into the renouncer's vow' and the epic-side gain are not in the Tamil.

Kannaki's release does wait on hearing the Buddha's dharma (அன்பு உறு மனத்தோடு அவன் அறம் கேட்டு ... பிறவி நீத்த பெற்றியம் ஆகுவம், 57-59), against Kural 10's பிறவிப் பெருங்கடல் crossed by reaching the Lord's feet. But the note's sea of births is line 40 of the previous unit, and teaches' 'replaces devotion with understanding' is untrue here: the unit makes worship of the Indra viharas (ஏத்துதலின், 55) save her from bad birth, and she hears with a loving mind.

Tirumanthiram 51 says the wise gave up தர்க்க வாதம் and gained release by reciting the Veda, holding that no dharma leaves out the Veda; Manimekalai 29:55-56 folds all other means of knowledge into inference (ஏனை அளவைகள் எல்லாம் ... அனுமானம் ஆம்) and teaches the five-membered syllogism on the road to dharma. Whether scripture stands above argument is a genuine incompatible claim.

The assemblies warn that if the festival is forgotten (விழாக்கோள் மறப்பின்) the spirit will bring affliction (இடும்பை செய்திடும்); in 25:197-199 the festival lapses (வானவன் விழாக் கோள் மா நகர் ஒழிந்தது) and Manimekala deity says அணி நகர் தன்னை அலை கடல் கொள்க. A warning and its fulfilment, with the punisher changed as teaches says.

Kural 555's tears (அழுதகண்ணீர்) wear away wealth slowly (தேய்க்கும்), and in the venba the king lost his life at her tears and words (கண்ணீரும் ... உண்டளவே தோற்றான் உயிர்); the contrast of slow and instant is specific. But this is a bridge with no gains clauses, so it cannot be sound as written.

Neelakesi 239 asks whether what the shaven-headed monks (இட்ட தலையராய்) recite from the Vinaya is the path of dharma; Kural 280 says shaving and long hair are not needed. 'Shaven-headed' describes the monks, it is not the content of the rule she attacks, so the contact is thin; teaches' 'the Jain one included' and the gain 'decides which order's discipline counts' are not in either text.

Silap 23:81 கடற்கடம்பெறிந்த காவலன் recalls Patitruppattu 11's felling of the guarded kadamba at the sea (பலர்மொசிந்து ஓம்பிய திரள்பூங் கடம்பின் கடியுடை முழுமுதல் துமிய): a real allusion. But the deed is kept as an epithet only, and teaches' 'the separate Cheras become one praised house' goes beyond Tamil that does not say whether the four வாழி lines name one king or several.

The foretold blessing வாய்வதாக நின் மனப்பாட்டு அறம் (21:171) returns in Manimekalai's own mouth at Kanchi, வாய்வது ஆக என் மனப்பாட்டு அறம் (28:244), as she casts off the borrowed form (மாயை விட்டு) the prophecy named. Prophecy and fulfilment in the same words.

The herdswomen wish the Pandya's drum victory day after day (வைகல் வைகல் மாறட்டு வெற்றி விளைப்பது), and in 20:83-88 the king, sceptre slack, calls himself the thief and falls: a reversal, and the irony teaches names is real. But a prayer for victory and the king's fall are not incompatible claims, so tension is the wrong type.

Bhutikan opens by calling her an unbeliever and a Sudra woman (நாத்திகம், சூத்திரி நீ) and at 852 concedes and is praised as one of the true (தத்துவரே நின்று). The arc is real but it is a reversal in the debate's story, not two incompatible claims, so tension does not fit.
links.text_issue: Verses 845-851 are missing, so the turn to the concession is lost; 826 lines 1 and 4 are hard to divide.

links.reason: The words meet: Manimekalai 17:1 பாத்தூண் ஏற்ற and யானைத்தீ நோய் (7) beside Kural 227 பாத்தூண் மரீஇயவனைப் பசியென்னும் தீப்பிணி, and Kayasandigai names her hunger the fruit of old deeds (பழ வினைப் பயத்தால்). But the epic says nothing of her own sharing, so the claimed limit on the couplet is constructed by the proposer; the couplet's அரிது already allows exceptions.

The phrase is shared exactly: Puram 173:4 ஊணொலி அரவம் for Pannan's house and Manimekalai 14:60 ஊண் ஒலி அரவம் ஒடுங்கியது ஆகி when Indra's rain leaves no hungry. The epic shows the patron's noisy kitchen falling silent when hunger ends, a condition the Sangam praise does not see, and both gains hold.

Kural 55 gives the wife who worships her husband command of the rain (பெய்யெனப் பெய்யும் மழை); the patikam says it was because she was a pathini (பத்தினி யாகலின்) that Kannaki brought ruin on the Pandya and fed Koodal to fire. The epic adds the destructive side of the same power, which the couplet does not suggest; the Silappathikaram itself takes up this couplet at 23:201.

Kural 557 likens the king's lack of grace to the world without rain (துளியின்மை ஞாலத்திற்கு ... வேந்தன் அளியின்மை); Kalittokai 10:5-7 likens the parched waste to the world under the shadow of a crooked-sceptred king (கோல் கோடியவன் நிழல் உலகு போல் உலறிய). Vehicle and tenor are swapped, and same_image fits.

Maasaathuvan renounced on hearing of the deaths and then knew wealth and body as not lasting (செல்வமும் யாக்கையும் நிலையா என்றே நிலைபெற உணர்ந்தே); Naladiyar 53 has the best renounce on seeing impermanence (நிலையாமை கண்டு). The grief-driven timing against மெல்ல is a modest contrast; the epic largely illustrates the quatrain, and qualifies is generous.
